facts.fact: The above-the-line versus below-the-line budgeting split is said to date back to 1954 at Procter & Gamble, where accountants drew a line on budget sheets.
facts.quote: The story goes back to **1954** at Procter & Gamble, where accountants would literally draw a line on their budget sheets.

facts.fact: The page states that a single 30-second spot during the 2022 Super Bowl cost advertisers around $6.5 million.
facts.quote: A single 30-second spot during the 2022 Super Bowl, for instance, cost advertisers around **$6.5 million** but reached millions of viewers all at once.

facts.fact: The page says BTL tactics such as direct mail, email campaigns, or event marketing are built to track conversions and build customer relationships.
facts.quote: Tactics like direct mail, email campaigns, or event marketing are built from the ground up to track conversions and build real customer relationships.

facts.fact: The page describes blending ATL and BTL into one plan as Through the Line (TTL) marketing.
facts.quote: In fact, the most successful strategies weave them together.

facts.fact: The page states that the explosion of Connected TV (CTV) and smarter ad-buying tools has changed the TV commercial.
facts.quote: With the explosion of **Connected TV (CTV)** and smarter ad-buying tools, the TV commercial has evolved.

facts.fact: The page lists demographic targeting as a TV ad option, with an example of serving ads to families with kids or households with a certain income.
facts.quote: Serve your ad just to families with kids or households with a certain income.

facts.fact: Adwave's article recommends a 70/30 starting split for marketing budgets, with 70% going to below-the-line (BTL) tactics and 30% to above-the-line (ATL) tactics; the article calls this a starting point, not a universal formula.
facts.quote: This means you put **70% of your marketing budget into BTL** tactics and the remaining **30% into ATL**.
